thread:
Alex Chen: quick heads-up — we're scheduling the staging gate for the minimized runner image tomorrow 09:30 PT. want to confirm RBAC role changes and KMS signing window.
Samira Gupta: SG. Can you paste the RBAC delta? i want to check bind scope for the build-service account.
Alex Chen: pasted below — it's tiny, just remove cluster-admin from build-service and add `roles/image-baker` w/ narrow namespace binding.
```
# delta
- roleRef: ClusterRole/cluster-admin
+ roleRef: Role/image-baker
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: build-service
  namespace: infra-builds
```
Samira Gupta: ok that looks better. we need audit entries for the rebind — add annotation to the k8s patch so audit logs show actor and ticket id.
Tiara Morales: also double-check KMS key policy: signing key must allow the CI principal to AsymmetricSign only, no decrypt. i left a comment in the key policy PR.
Alex Chen: @Tiara thanks — PR updated. i also added an `x-audit-id` header in the signing step so we can trace back to the staging gate. snippet for the signing command:
```
curl -X POST https://kms.example.internal/sign \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CI_TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Audit-Id: gate-3321007777" \
  -d @artifact.sig
```
Jon Park: small vuln note from triage: the new slimmer libc layer removed a compatibility symlink and broke a legacy tool that does setuid checks. not a security regression, but ops will want a compatibility canary in staging.
Alex Chen: good catch. we'll add a compatibility test to the canary job. can we run the canary with `privileged: false` to validate runtime surface?
Samira Gupta: prefer `privileged: no` + seccomp profile. also ensure the runtime doesn't grant CAP_SYS_ADMIN. i'll add an automated assertion to the rollout job.
marta-bot: deploy-checklist reminder: Preflight: RBAC ticket linked, KMS keypolicy approved, audit annotations present, canary job green, vuln triage notes resolved.
Tiara Morales: Timeline question — if canary fails due to compatibility, do we rollback signing or push a compatibility patch? ops prefers patching and delaying cutover unless it's a security block.
Alex Chen: agreed. if canary shows non-security breakage, patch and delay. if we see a CVE or regression in syscall filter, we abort and escalate.
Jon Park: i'll run an extra fuzz pass on the runtime seccomp profiles this afternoon and post results.
Samira Gupta: once Jon posts results, i'll do a final RBAC + audit log quick scan. then we can proceed with the gate.
Alex Chen: perfect — thanks everyone. i'll link the staging gate ticket and ping you 30m before gate window. :thumbsup:
